episodes.title: The AI Investment Boom Goes Beyond America
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
PIMCO examines how the global AI infrastructure investment boom is propping up growth across the US and Asia while building a new source of cyclical concentration risk. The analysis matters for EM traders because much of the AI capex impulse is being exported via trade and supply chains to Asia, and a slowdown in investment growth (not just a collapse) would hit global demand.

**Key points**
- Announced 2026 US tech capex points to over $1 trillion, with ~$1.5 trillion more forecast thereafter.
- AI investment has directly added only ~0.4 percentage point to US annualized GDP growth since early 2025 (out of ~2% growth) because of high import content, but contributed ~1.2 points to the 2.7% growth in US domestic demand.
- Equity wealth effects from AI optimism add an estimated 0.5-0.7 percentage point to growth, 1-1.5x the direct investment impulse.
- AI-related export exposure is equivalent to roughly 30% of GDP for Taiwan and over 15% for South Korea; Mexico is also a key node in the North American AI supply chain.
- China and Middle East economies are increasingly building their own AI infrastructure, broadening the cycle beyond the US.
- Global production of computers/electronics is exceptionally strong even as broader industrial production growth stays muted.

**FX / rates implications**
- Taiwan (TWD) and South Korea (KRW) have outsized sensitivity to any deceleration in US AI capex growth given export exposure near 15-30% of GDP — watch for spillover into export data and currency performance.
- Mexico (MXN) carries supply-chain linked AI exposure through the North American tech/nearshoring channel.
- The equity wealth channel ties US AI sentiment to broader risk-on flows that support EM carry trades when US stocks are strong; a reversal in AI-driven equity valuations would tighten financial conditions and pressure EM FX broadly via risk-off USD demand.
- China's own AI infrastructure buildout is an independent growth support that could offset some of the trade-channel risk if US demand fades.

**Watch list**
- Signs of deceleration in the growth rate (not just level) of US AI capex announcements/filings, which would reduce the global growth impulse.
- Taiwan and South Korea export/tech production data as a leading indicator of AI cycle turns.
- US equity valuations and productivity realization, since a stall without productivity payoff could trigger a financial-conditions tightening that spreads to EM.
